topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture and outlines its focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate Immune Sensing: PAMPs, DAMPs, and Self-Discrimination
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the molecular signatures of pathogens and tissue damage that trigger innate immunity while distinguishing self from non-self.

topics.label: Pattern Recognition Receptors and Inflammatory Signaling Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the localization, families, and intracellular signaling mechanisms of host receptors that detect danger signals, including TLRs and the inflammasome.

topics.label: Inflammatory Execution: Cell Trafficking, Lymphatic Transport, and Systemic Consequences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the cellular mechanisms that mobilize immune cells to tissues and lymph nodes, as well as the pathological outcomes of runaway systemic inflammation.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Containment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how inflammatory responses are shut down, how damaged tissues are repaired, and how persistent threats are contained in chronic lesions.

topics.label: Lecture Closing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the session and previews the upcoming lecture on the complement system.
